notes_for_editor: Story rests mainly on the 2003 NRHP nomination (which cites Hurley and Taylor, not read directly) plus the USLHS roster. No Lighthouse Board annual-report text found in corpus for 1881/1903 (corpus lacks those volumes); the 1881 quote is the nomination's quote of the board. Tower height conflict: nomination says 50 ft tower / 64 ft with lantern; LHB 1894 says 58 ft. USLHS keeper dates differ from NRHP for Grimm (1892-1905 vs 1891-1906); USLHS first entry 'Myles J. Thompson (560-560)' is junk and omitted. USLHS lists Thomas John O'Hagan as head keeper 1925-1954; the NRHP calls him Thomas J. and the elder Thomas P. Jane M. Donnelly, Eric C. Awkerman etc. taken straight from the roster. Christopher Morse/George Latham: not linked to Amos Latham without a source. Wartime keepers per NRHP (McGlne, Parker, Randall, Woodland) matched to roster by name only. The 'Francis Woodward' roster line is 'at least 1961-1962'. No wreck/rescue narratives found; Life-Saving and newspaper searches not run (budget; thin on wreck material). Listing date of NRHP (2003 per record) not stated in story. Fact-check 2026-10-27: year of the report at scan p.649 of annualreportlig01statgoog is not confirmed (volume is 1893-94; text speaks of July 1893), so it is cited as the 1893-94 volume; it calls the site 'lowland' and 107 ft focal height, the nomination a knoll 59 ft above sea level.
